cohort: 128 women in their first seven months after childbirth
finding: Vaginal birth was associated with reduced pelvic floor muscle strength, while caesarean section had a protective effect; urinary incontinence during pregnancy predicted urinary incontinence after childbirth, and women with previous pregnancies and heavier newborns were more likely to experience it.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth predisposed women to reduced pelvic floor muscle strength, while caesarean section had a protective effect against it.
followup_time: Within the first seven months after childbirth
birth_weight: Higher newborn weight was associated with increased risk of urinary incontinence after childbirth
